newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - AUGUST 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - AUGUST 14.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Mineral and Energy Minister Penuell Maduna has renewed his attack on Auditor-Geneal Henri Kluever, repeating an allegation that the 170 million rand "loss" from South Africa's strategic oil stock had been "neatly tucked away" and raising questions over his membership of auditing organisations.

- It would take at least 10 years to build the necessary management skills in the public service because of the chaotic state of administration in the provinces, public service director-general Paseka Ncholo said on Wednesday.
- Three black empowerment groups are poised to take a multimillion-rand take in the company formed through the merger of Persetel and Q Data.

- Kopano Ke Matla - the Congress of South African Trade Unions' (Cosatu's) investment company - and a Danish Labour Federation subsidiary plan to put in joint bid for Aventura, the state-owned holiday company, which is likely to be sold later this year.
- The nation's assets - from toilet seats and door knobs to computers and printers - are being stripped from Parliament by audacious thieves, who recently also made off with 20 kg of sausages.

- The South African Democratic Teachers' Union had accepted in principle government's final offer of increases for teachers ranging from 8 percent to 11 percent, the education department said on Wednesday.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Documents released at a press briefing on Wednesday by Penuell Maduna, the mineral and energy minister, paint a picture of widespread irregularities in the state's oil purchasing arm, the Central Energy Fund (CEF).
- Q Data, the information technology company posted a 36 percent rise in headline earnings to 28.6 cents a share in the year to June 30 from 21 cents in same period last year.

- Amalgamated Beverage Industries and a black consortium were the lead bidders for New Age Beverages (NAB) bottling plant, and have made offers of 90 million rand and 100 million rand respectively, an industry source said on Wednesday.

- Hoechst's polyester fibre operation in the Western Cape and Durban Fibres, which it bought from the Frame Group in 1993 and recently invested 205 million rand in upgrading, could be sold to the Coastal Group, industry sources said on Wednesday.

- At least 53 clothing manufactureres in KwaZulu-Natal had deducted nearly 10 million rand in provident and heathcare fund contributions, union subscriptions and council levies from workers' salaries, but had failed to pay them to the local clothing sector bargaining council, according to a recent survey by the South African Clothing and Textile Worker's Union (Sactwu).
SAKE BEELD
- Q Data, which will soon merge with Persetel, lifted earnings 36 percent to 28.6 cents a share in the year to June.
- Drastic proposals aimed at turning Gauteng into a telecommunications and technology centre form part of a trade and industrial strategy which was unveiled on Wednesday.
THE STAR

- The Congo soccer squad fired the first psychological salvo in an already tense war of nerves on arrival at Johannesburg airport on Wednesday when they refused to accept accommodation at a central Johannesburg hotel arranged by the South African Football Association.

- The late Conservative Party leader Dr Andries Treurnicht unwittingly gave his blessing for the assassination of Chris Hani by providing Clive Derby-Lewis with biblical justification for murder, the Truth and Reconciliation Commission heard on Wedensday.
- Four men, wanted in connection with last month's 17-million rand lion highway heist, handed themselves over to police on Wednesday and were released after a few hours.
- Gauteng's intensified credit control campaign has netted 500 million rand in arrears since councils started cutting off electricity last Monday.
